Native launch continuity

The system launch frame and session restore are now a quiet grouped background that matches Home. The Motion W lockup stays on sign-in, where Apple allows a splash after launch completes.

After-only fixture evidence

iPhone 16 Pro (27.0) UDID E055DEBC-12B1-4E0F-BE11-1CFFF4A454DE, WisconsinPerformance launch-view / login. No matched before pair from this checkout: the previous branded still lived in the system UILaunchScreen and the launch-view fixture, and those PNGs were not retained beside the earlier review. The reported 9:30 still is included as a device screenshot at a different pixel size, not as a hash-matched pair.

What changed, and why

System launch frame

Was

LaunchBackground #140B10 plus a centered LaunchLockup wordmark, which read as a purple splash.

Now

UILaunchScreen is a required iOS 27 color-only frame. LaunchBackground matches system grouped (light #F2F2F7, dark #000000). No image.

Session restore

Was

LaunchView continued the crimson scene and raster lockup, so the first SwiftUI frame was also a splash.

Now

LaunchView is Color(.systemGroupedBackground) with delayed Checking your session copy. Optimistic sessions still skip it.

App switcher

Was

WindowLaunchStillHost covered the live UI with the same branded still.

Now

Inactive snapshots show the live UI. No privacy lock and no splash overlay.

Sign-in and kiosk

Was

Kiosk cold launch and resume used the same Motion W still.

Now

Login and password setup keep the crimson lockup. Kiosk launch uses KioskLaunchBackground #0B0B0D; resume is labeled progress on the existing backdrop.

Things to know

  • The launch-view captures include Checking your session because the fixture waits through the delayed progress reveal. The system UILaunchScreen itself has no spinner or text.
  • Physical-device app-switcher and managed-iPad kiosk visual proof remain open.
  • No commit or push.
